methodology: All three candidates measured on the SAME 22 real development cases (Candidate C measured twice: v1 with a naive numeric regex, v2 after fixing a real word-boundary defect found in v1). Candidate A/B additionally measured on 5 validation cases. Phase-7 held-out untouched during this comparison.

candidate_a_deterministic.architecture: numeric exact-match + lexical word-overlap, no LLM call

candidate_b_semantic_judge.architecture: single Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b strict-JSON-schema call judging the whole claim + all cited Evidence together
candidate_b_semantic_judge.note: 22/22 dev + 5/5 validation AFTER a real prompt fix (see failure analysis F1: judge was using outside biomedical/regulatory knowledge to call CONTRADICTED instead of PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED when Evidence simply didn't address the overclaimed part). Before the fix: 20/22 dev.

candidate_c_hybrid.architecture: deterministic numeric precheck (hard override) + Candidate B semantic judge
candidate_c_hybrid.real_defect_found: the deterministic numeric-mismatch check is asymmetric between free-prose claim text (numbers separated by spaces, e.g. 'Phase 2') and compact enum-style Evidence field values (e.g. 'PHASE2', 'CHEMBL941') - even after fixing v1's worse defect (treating digits embedded in NCT/ChEMBL identifiers as claimed numeric facts), the extraction still misses digits glued to letters on the EVIDENCE side, causing false CONTRADICTED overrides on otherwise-correct claims.
candidate_c_hybrid.decision: NOT SELECTED - Candidate B alone already reaches 100% dev+validation without this fragility; not worth further engineering effort for a candidate that is not going to be chosen.

selection_reason: Highest accuracy (100% dev+validation after the one real prompt fix), simplest architecture (no extra deterministic layer to introduce new failure modes), and the found Candidate-C defect demonstrates that a naive deterministic layer is actively harmful here, not merely unnecessary.
